title: Which model runs what
ask: Which model, effort and spending cap should each kind of Claude run use?
why: Until today every run the app started used your account's default model at its default effort (claude-fable-5-1 at xhigh) - a one-tick Apply the same as a design review - and shared your own session budget; the 2026-09-25 Apply for A1-A4 failed on that limit. The app now sets the model, effort and a spending cap per kind of run, and you can change them in Settings at any time. Ticks, values, choices and drives are applied by rx7.py with no model at all. What ships today: Apply answers and parts rounds on sonnet at medium effort with a 2 USD cap; Plan, review and new projects on the account default at high effort with an 8 USD cap; if the default model is unavailable the run falls back to sonnet. This is money, so the choice is yours.
options:
(a) Keep the shipped defaults: sonnet at medium for applying answers and parts rounds, the account default at high for plan, review and new projects. Cheapest safe mix; an apply run follows a playbook and needs no design judgement.
(b) Everything on the account default at high effort. Every run at full quality; every tick that reaches Claude costs as much as a design run and draws on your session budget.
(c) Everything on sonnet at medium. Cheapest of all; design rows and reviews may be weaker and need a second pass.
(d) Your own mix: set it in Settings and say so here in words.
recommend: (a), unless an Apply run on sonnet ever applies one of your answers wrongly - then (b) for those runs too.
stops: Nothing: the shipped defaults are live now. Your answer fixes them or changes them.

title: How much the plan work may spend
ask: How much may Plan everything ready spend, and may it start without your press?
why: Thirty-odd agent rows are READY across the projects (verify 17, engine 12, beauty 3, luxury 1 today) and nothing starts them: a Plan run begins only when you press Plan on a project page. The Projects hub now has one button, Plan everything ready, that queues one Plan run per project with rows Claude can start, each under the design-run spending cap in Settings (8 USD today). Each run also draws on your subscription's session budget, which is the limit that stopped auto-apply on 2026-09-25. How much the plan work may spend in one go, and whether it may start itself on a timer instead of your press, is money and yours.
options:
(a) Press the button when you want the queue worked, with the per-run cap in Settings as the only limit. Nothing spends without a press; the queue waits between your visits.
(b) A cap per press: the button stops queueing runs once the caps add up to a total you name (say 20 USD), and says how many rows it left. Your press, a known ceiling.
(c) Start on a timer: the desktop runs Plan everything ready once a day when the app is open, under a daily total you name. Rows are worked without a press; the session budget is shared with your own use that day.
recommend: (a), unless you find yourself pressing it every time you open the app - then (c) with a daily total you are happy to see gone.
stops: Nothing: the button works today under the per-run cap. Your answer sets the ceiling, or a timer.

title: Where the phone reads the record from
ask: Should the phone keep computing the record itself in WebAssembly, or fetch the export the GitHub Action can publish on every push?
why: The phone reads the record by fetching every CSV from GitHub (127 files, 2.7 MB on the first sync) and running the real rx7.py inside the app in WebAssembly (Pyodide, 13 MB) to compute what it shows - the same export the desktop computes in 0.7 s takes several times that on a phone, and the engine has to be compiled at the first sync. The pitch sold this as "one tool, not two copies of the rules", and that is true. The other way to keep it true: the GitHub Action that already runs rx7.py check on every push also runs rx7.py export and publishes the result (0.85 MB gzipped) as a release asset, outside the tree so D-405 holds; the phone fetches that one file, shows it at once, and keeps Pyodide only for the one thing it writes (the answer file, checked by rx7.py's own inbox_entry). Same rules, one place they run. Changing where the phone reads from is scope, so it is your call. Since 2026-09-26 the phone already skips the export when a commit touched no record file and loads the engine only when it needs it, so the everyday cost is lower either way.
options:
(a) Keep it as designed: the phone runs rx7.py itself. No new moving part; every sync that changes a record file costs a WebAssembly export (tens of seconds on a phone, to be measured on your Galaxy once installed), and the APK carries the 13 MB engine.
(b) CI publishes the export: the record job on GitHub runs rx7.py export on every push and attaches export.json to a rolling release; the phone fetches that one file (about 1 MB) and shows it at once, and runs rx7.py in WebAssembly only to write an answer. Needs the Action to have write permission on releases; if the Action ever fails, the phone shows the last export it fetched and says how old it is.
(c) Both: the phone fetches the published export when it is there and falls back to computing it when it is not. The most resilient and the most code.
recommend: (b), unless you would rather the phone depend on nothing but the repository itself - then (a), and we measure the sync time on the Galaxy first.
stops: Nothing today: the phone works as designed. Your answer decides whether plan step P39's CI publishing is built.

title: Terminals in the Manual
ask: Should the Manual show a part's terminals from the 1982 wiring diagram, labelled as unchecked, or keep hiding them until each is metered on the car?
why: The wave-1 research read the 1982 wiring diagram and wrote 426 terminal rows for 86 electrical parts: each terminal's label, what it does, the factory wire colour on it and where that wire goes. Every one of them carries 'confirm', because by R11 nothing about the car counts as checked until it is metered on the car - and the Manual therefore shows none of them. What you see today on a part's page is one line: '5 terminals recorded from the 1982 diagram, held back until checked on the car'. The wiring-check rows that would clear them are the 80 rows block VER.02 asks about, and the harness they describe is being replaced. So the terminals are either shown as what they are - the factory diagram's claim, labelled so - or they stay a counter and waves 2 and 3 stop spending research on terminals nobody will see. This is what the Manual asserts about your car, your bar (spec answer 4.5).
options:
(a) Show them, labelled: each electrical part's page gets its terminal table under the heading 'From the 1982 wiring diagram - not checked on this car', and a checked one (a wiring row done, or a terminal metered during the build) loses the label. The Manual states its source instead of hiding the fact; waves 2 and 3 keep recording terminals.
(b) Hide them until checked, as now, and stop recording terminals in waves 2 and 3 (tokens saved; the 426 stay in the record for the electrical build to use).
(c) Hide them until checked, and keep recording them in waves 2 and 3 for the build's sake, knowing the Manual will not show them until the new harness is in.
recommend: (a), unless you want the Manual to show only what you have seen with your own meter - then (b), which also stops spending research on them.
stops: Plan step P40's part-page table, and whether waves 2 and 3 of the research record terminals.
